chunks: “If a group prays while between them and the Imam there is that which cannot be crossed, then that Imam is not an Imam for them. And whichever row, whose people are praying by the prayer of an Imam, has between them and the row that is ahead of them that which cannot be crossed, then that is not a prayer for them. And if it is a curtain or a wall, then that is not a prayer for them, except for one who is opposite the door.”
He said: And he said: “These enclosures were only introduced by the tyrants, and there is no prayer for one who prays behind them, following the prayer of those within them.”
He said: And he said: “Any woman who prays behind an Imam, while between her and him there is that which cannot be crossed, then that is not a prayer for her.”
He said: I said, “If a person comes wanting to pray, how should he act while she is at the side of the man?” He said: “He enters between her and the man, and she moves back a little.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the prayer leader being followed in congregational salat
key_terms.الْمَقَاصِيرُ: enclosed prayer spaces or screened-off areas
key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman worshipper mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.جِدَارًا: a wall separating worshippers from the Imam or prior row
key_terms.سِتْرًا: a barrier or covering that obstructs connection
key_terms.صَفٍّ: a row of worshippers in congregational prayer
key_terms.مَا لَا يُتَخَطَّى: a gap or separation that cannot be crossed
key_terms.مُقْتَدِيًا: following the Imam in congregational prayer

ai.seo_question: What breaks continuity in congregational prayer behind the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith sets legal conditions for valid congregational salat, especially the continuity of rows and the absence of obstructive barriers between the Imam and followers. It also addresses the ruling of praying behind enclosed structures and gives a practical instruction about row arrangement when a woman is beside a man.
